extracted.intended_audience: journalists and health-care consumers (and others who evaluate health news/PR)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level standards and operating principles used by HealthNewsReview.org for evaluating health care journalism, news releases, advertising, marketing and PR; intended to help consumers and journalists critically analyze health care claims and improve the quality of health reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve public dialogue by helping consumers critically analyze claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission is to improve the public dialogue about health care by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be oriented toward enabling consumers to question and evaluate claims made about interventions rather than merely repeating promotional language. Emphasize critical thinking about asserted benefits, harms, evidence strength, and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote shared decision-making with accurate, balanced, complete information about tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should check whether a story or release provides balanced presentation of benefits and harms, quantifies tradeoffs where possible, and frames information to support decisions made jointly between patients and clinicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate journalism, advertising, marketing, PR and other consumer-directed messages
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of review includes not only news stories but promotional materials and PR — all items that could affect consumer perceptions and decisions. Reviewers should apply similar critical standards across these message types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry influence
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org does not accept advertising, nor funding from any entity whose support would represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and disclose independence: avoid funding sources that could influence content. State funding relationships openly and ensure that no commercial supporter has editorial input. This independence underpins credibility of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert contributors must avoid conflicts of interest and disclosures when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: All expert contributors to the project pledge that they do not accept payments from drug or device companies or from any commercial entity whose support might represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit independent experts; when quoting external experts who are not team members, ask about financial interests and disclose relevant ties in the article. Use and maintain a list of industry-independent experts for journalists to consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: No editorial input from funders
rubrics_metrics.description: No funder ever had any editorial input into the operation of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain explicit separation between funders and editorial decision-making. State this policy publicly to reinforce trust in impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a provider of medical advice or advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org is not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science. We don’t give medical advice. We are not an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about role limitations in reviews and communications: critiques are educational and evaluative, not clinical recommendations or advocacy campaigns. Avoid presenting reviews as medical advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about scope and resource limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The site acknowledges limits set by a small editorial staff and budget and that it can’t review every story or promotional message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate operational constraints clearly to users. Triage review choices and be transparent about selection criteria or why certain items are not reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide consumer-facing criteria and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish concrete, user-friendly checklists, toolkits or tips so consumers and journalists can apply the same standards in assessing health claims (e.g., questions about evidence strength, absolute vs relative effects, harms, costs, alternatives).
